Quick tech snapshot from initial investigation:
- v7b-q3 uses an aggressive per-layer 4-bit quant profile with a new fused attention kernel on A100s.
- We see ~2.8x increase in tail KV cache invalidations for PinnaclePay's request shape (short prompts, high concurrency). That leads to frequent cache reloads which blow up latency and backpressure.
- Error log correlation: ~72% of 5xx originates from the new attention kernel path hitting an unhandled precision edge case in multi-head normalization.

Actions in flight:
1) Rolling back PinnaclePay's dedicated pool to the previous quant profile (started 16:30 PT).
2) Isolating a failing request sample to reproduce locally.
3) Feature-flagging the fused kernel to opt-out while we patch normalization handling.

I'll post a short repro in the shared thread when available.

—Markus
VP, Serving Runtime

- Opt-out fused kernel via feature flag: in flight (will be applied to PinnaclePay pool within 30m).
- Repro and patch: Markus/Karthik to prioritize a normalization-edge-case fix; target hotfix within 48 hours.

Ask for execs:
- Approve a one-time credit (estimate: $12k) to PinnaclePay for today's operational impact.
- Priority engineering headcount allocation for the patch (2 sprints over next 2 weeks).
- Sign-off to delay v7b-q3 wider rollout until we validate kernel stability across short-prompt workloads.

I'll attach a short customer-facing note after exec sign-off.

—Vanessa
